scenes.headline: Skills: package your expertise
scenes.sub: Teach the agent a job once. It remembers forever.
lines: Lesson four. Skills.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
If you've explained a process three times, it should be a skill.

scenes.headline: One job, done your way.
lines: A skill teaches the agent one job, done your way.

lines.cap: It's a folder, with one markdown file inside, called SKILL.md.

scenes.headline: Name. Description. Steps.
lines: At the top, a name, and a description.
The description is how the agent decides when to use it.
Below that, the steps, in plain language.
scenes.code:
---
name: pdf-report
description: Build a branded PDF report
  from a CSV. Use when asked for a
  report or a one-pager.
---

1. Summarise the 3 key trends
2. Fill templates/report.html
3. Export to PDF

highlights.label: Trigger
highlights.note: The description decides when it fires

scenes.headline: Only pay for what's needed.
lines: Skills scale because of progressive disclosure.
At first, the agent only sees the name and description.
The full steps load only when a request matches.
And long references live in separate files, read only when needed.

scenes.headline: Descriptions that trigger.
lines: If a skill doesn't fire, the description is usually the problem.
Say what it does.
Say when to use it.
And use the words people actually type.

scenes.headline: Same file. Everywhere.
lines: The skill format is an open standard.
Put it in your project, keep it in your personal folder, or add it in the Claude app.
Write it once, and it travels with you.

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, and the description decides when it fires.
Your mission: turn the process you explain most often into your first skill.
